title: Walker circulation controls ENSO atmospheric feedbacks in uncoupled and coupled climate model simulations
problem: Many climate models strongly underestimate key ENSO atmospheric feedbacks (zonal wind and surface heat flux), which hampers the realistic simulation of ENSO dynamics and is linked to biases in the atmospheric mean state and equatorial sea surface temperatures.
method: This study conducts sensitivity experiments with a single atmosphere model, in which an average equatorial SST bias is added to the observed SST forcing, to demonstrate how this bias weakens the atmospheric mean state and the resulting ENSO atmospheric feedbacks.
task: The task is to investigate how the mean state of the Pacific Walker Circulation and sea surface temperature biases control the strength of ENSO atmospheric feedbacks in uncoupled and coupled climate models, explaining why these feedbacks are often underestimated.

innovation: This paper demonstrates that the underestimation of ENSO atmospheric feedbacks in climate models is controlled by a weakened Pacific Walker Circulation, which in turn is caused by a common equatorial cold sea surface temperature bias.

The Pacific Walker Circulation (PWC) is an equatorial zonal circulation cell that arises from the zonal sea surface temperature (SST) difference between the cold tongue region in the eastern equatorial Pacific (EEP) and the warm pool region in the western equatorial Pacific (WEP) (Philander 1990).
